title: Optimal symmetric rendezvous among discrete locations
aliases: symmetric rendezvous on the complete graph
decision_reason: Explicit problem, independent August 2026 status, exact strategy/time conventions, theorem-scope comparisons and separated A32 self-pass passed.

problem_fingerprint.model_or_objects: Two independent draws from one probability law on infinite location sequences; an independent uniform fixed permutation matches private labels.
problem_fingerprint.dimension: No spatial dimension; n discrete locations.
problem_fingerprint.domain: [n] at each integer time in N0.
problem_fingerprint.regularity_and_data_class: All probability laws on the product sigma-algebra; arbitrary memory and within-agent temporal dependence.
problem_fingerprint.boundary_or_initial_conditions: First visit at time zero; no conditioning on initially distinct locations.
problem_fingerprint.parameter_range: Every integer n≥4, counted as one family.
problem_fingerprint.quantifiers: For each n determine the infimum over all common strategies.
problem_fingerprint.normalization: One simultaneous visit per unit time; meeting at time zero has cost zero.
problem_fingerprint.observable_or_norm: Expected first time at the same physical location.
problem_fingerprint.limit_regime_and_order: Exact finite-n values; asymptotic bounds are context, not an assumed limit.
problem_fingerprint.computational_model_and_dependencies: No computational or memory restriction; no tokens, shared random bits, common labels or assigned roles.

statement_source_and_scope_match: A13 Problem 5 states the family. CFK26 §2 gives the sequence/permutation model used here. The draft asks for its infimum value without imposing the later section's block strategies or asserting attainment.
proposed_statement_text: For iid X,Y with arbitrary common law μ on [n]^N0 and an independent uniform fixed π∈Sn, determine infμ E[inf{t≥0:π(Xt)=Yt}] for every n≥4.
applied_significance: Delay of anonymous decentralized coordination: simultaneous terminal selection under an unknown matching and common-channel attempts. Synchronization and equal travel cost are explicit modeling assumptions.
